findings.description: Satisfied. All three suites exit 0, and the issue's reproduction, rebuilt by hand rather than reused from the suite, reports frontmatter-key-domain naming the file and both keys, with no frontmatter-budget line for it.
findings.evidence:
bash tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh -> exit=0 ("inbox-to-memory smoke: ok"); tests/file-issue-smoke.sh -> exit=0; tests/handoff-smoke.sh -> exit=0. Hand-built 20-key record, closing fence measured at line 21 (awk 'NR>1 && $0=="---"{print NR;exit}' -> 21), linted by the shipped inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh:

findings.description: Satisfied. The suite pins an inline scope whose frontmatter closes on line 21 and asserts both halves (key-domain reported, budget refuted), and the assertion discriminates: moving the check after the budget guard on a scratch copy of the tree turns the suite red.
findings.evidence:
tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:186-227 builds $overrun_scope with a record whose fence closes on line 21, then asserts:
  require_failure "$overrun_out" "FAIL $overrun_file: frontmatter-key-domain: carries both \`tags\` and \`themes\`"
  refute_failure "$overrun_out" "frontmatter-budget"
refute_failure (tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:85-94) is a real negative assertion: it greps the output and exits 1 on a matching ^FAIL line.
Mutation, run on rsync copy of the tree at <scratch>/mutant with the key-domain block (lint-scope.sh:159-168) relocated to sit after the budget guard (lint-scope.sh:170-173):
  bash <scratch>/mutant/tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh -> exit=1
  "lint did not report the failure: FAIL /private/tmp/i2m-overrun.B1dOaR/_memory/decisions/tags-and-themes-both-populated-Kx3fQ7pRtN.md: frontmatter-key-domain: carries both `tags` and `themes`"
  "FAIL ...Kx3fQ7pRtN.md: frontmatter-budget: closing --- on line 21, past the 20-line budget"
The mutation was confined to the copy; `git status --porcelain` at the end of the check still shows only the worker's three paths, and `git diff --stat -- inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh` still reads 14 insertions / 3 deletions, unchanged from the start of the check.

findings.description: Satisfied, and I rule explicitly on the worker's claim that pre-existing assertions cover both cases: they do, and neither is vacuous. The clause asks whether the suite asserts the two passing cases, not whether this task added new fixtures for them, and both carrying files are v2 files the lint actually checks.
findings.evidence:
Journal half: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:708 `require_line "$jrn_lint" "failures: 0" journal-migrated` lints $jrn, the scope produced by running the migrator over journal-v1 with --apply. Reproduced by hand: the migrated entry carries `schema: 2` (line 2), `memory_type: Journal` (line 5), `themes: [governance, delivery-risk]` (line 12) and no `tags:` line; shipped lint reports `v2 files: 1` / `failures: 0`, so the file is linted rather than skipped. Discrimination: a scratch-copy mutant firing on memory_type (`themes` present AND `memory_type: Journal`) reports `FAIL .../6SMjpofI2b.md: frontmatter-key-domain` / `failures: 1` on that same scope, so :708 would go red.
Record half: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:184 `refute_failure "$broken_out" "vendor-lock-window-WJicoHVdFw.md"`. tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/broken/_memory/decisions/vendor-lock-window-WJicoHVdFw.md:1-13 carries `schema: 2`, `memory_type: Decision`, `tags: [vendor]` and no `themes`. Shipped lint on the broken scope emits no ^FAIL line naming it (grep of the captured output, tested with `test -z`). Discrimination: a mutant firing on `tags` alone produces `FAIL .../vendor-lock-window-WJicoHVdFw.md: frontmatter-key-domain`, breaking the refute.
Neither assertion rests on the unmigrated journal-v1 fixture the lint skips.

findings.description: Satisfied, including the masked-second-defect trap. The fixture sits under broken/, carries memory_type so it routes to RECORD_KEY_ORDER, holds exactly one defect, and both the arithmetic and the comment that explains it were updated.
findings.evidence:
tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/broken/_memory/decisions/tags-themes-mixup-9YpQ2xLmZk.md:1-11 -- keys in order: schema, id, memory_type (Decision), title, status, date, last_confirmed, tags, themes. Every one appears in RECORD_KEY_ORDER (lint-scope.sh:21) and in contract sequence. Fence closes on line 11, under the 20-line budget.
One defect, proved rather than inferred: linted alone the shipped lint reports exactly `FAIL .../tags-themes-mixup-9YpQ2xLmZk.md: frontmatter-key-domain: ...` / `failures: 1`. With the key-domain condition neutered to `if false; then` on the scratch copy -- which unmasks anything the check's early `return` at lint-scope.sh:167 would hide -- the same scope reports `v2 files: 1` / `failures: 0`, and the broken scope emits no failure naming the fixture at all. There is no second defect behind the first.
Arithmetic: shipped lint on tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/broken reports `v2 files: 20` / `failures: 19`, matching tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:157-158 (`v2 files: 19`->20, `failures: 18`->19 in the diff against d4ce6d2).
Comment: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:150-155 no longer calls the scope's lone record defect-free. It now reads "the arithmetic still lands one short of the file count: vendor-lock-window is link bait for the contradiction check and stays clean; every other v2 file here, including the new tags/themes record, carries exactly one planted defect" -- true of 20 files and 19 failures. The companion comment at :182-183 was moved from "eighteenth" to "twentieth defect nobody planted", also correct at 19 planted defects.

findings.description: Satisfied, and I rule explicitly on the worker's claim about the comm -23 output: the two base lines that fail to appear in the current set are the same two call sites with updated numbers, which C-6 required, not deletions. Nothing else vanished, and no helper was weakened.
findings.evidence:
Assertion sets extracted from each suite at d4ce6d2 and from the working copy, sorted:
  inbox-to-memory-smoke: base=202 cur=207.
  comm -23 (in base, absent from current), the complete output:
    require_line "$broken_out" "failures: 18" broken
    require_line "$broken_out" "v2 files: 19" broken
  comm -13 (added): 7 lines, including require_line "$broken_out" "v2 files: 20" broken and require_line "$broken_out" "failures: 19" broken.
  file-issue-smoke: base=41 cur=41, comm -23 empty. handoff-smoke: base=28 cur=28, comm -23 empty.
Ruling on those two: `git diff --no-color -U3 d4ce6d2 -- tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` shows them replaced in place inside one hunk at :157-158, same output variable ($broken_out), same label (broken), same helper (require_line, still an exact -Fqx match). The call sites still run and still assert the broken scope's arithmetic; only the literals moved, which is exactly what C-6's check demands and what C-7's own failing example contrasts against ("deleted rather than updated"). Neither a removal nor a loosening.
No assertion hid behind those two: 202 - 2 + 7 = 207 reconciles the counts, the diff touches only two hunks (@@ -150,13 and @@ -180,11), and none of the require_*/refute_* helper definitions (tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:14-99) appear in it.
All three suites exit 0.

findings.description: Satisfied. The failure message and every comment this task adds or rewrites explain why rather than restating the code, and none of the named tells appear. One nit, below the bar for a finding against the clause: "this check exists for/to fix" recurs three times across the added prose, and "the new tags/themes record" is diff-anchored (humanizer pattern 30), though the suite's existing voice already does the same at :756 ("The seam T-001 planted").
findings.evidence:

  lint-scope.sh:166 failure string: "carries both `tags` and `themes`, a record's key and a journal entry's" -- names both keys and the confusion behind them, matching the sibling shape at lint-scope.sh:133 and :171.
